# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall (clip-on): Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 on sale (list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick for clear sound, a comfortable clip that doesn't bounce, and easy controls. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Downsides: only IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and they can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic. Runner's World also says Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- Buy: [Runner's World guide, with Bose/Amazon/Walmart links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, with listings around $125 at REI and Best Buy**
- Your ears stay the most open, and the battery lasts about 12 hours. It has IP55 water resistance and physical buttons.
- The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats. WIRED found the sound bassy but a bit less clear than the older OpenRun.
- Buy: [WIRED review, with Amazon/REI/Best Buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating. WIRED named it best overall, and Runner's World picked it for long runs.
- Buy: [WIRED's best open earbuds guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, $79.99 to $129.99 depending on the retailer**
- SoundGuys calls it the best budget pick. It has 10 hours per buds charge (42 with the case), IP55 water resistance, and a secure ear hook.
- Dealectric reports that code AFSC20 took $25.99 off at Soundcore's store on Oct 22. The code is for full-price items and expires 12/31/2026, so confirm it at checkout.
- Buy: [Soundcore AeroFit 2 via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2). SoundGuys also lists it at Amazon: [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best on a tight budget: JLab Flex Open, about $40**
- It's a low-risk way to see whether clip-ons suit you. The sound is less detailed than on pricier pairs, and the controls are touch-only. The SoundPeats PearlClip Pro (about $50) is a similar WIRED pick.
- Buy: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Also good:** The Nothing Ear (Open) was SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick and their best for running. It has an IP54 rating and strong bass for the category, and it was $99 at Amazon in the listing ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).

**How to choose**
- **Maximum awareness, and you don't mind a neckband:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound in a clip-on:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Marathon-length battery and rain or sweat:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Budget:** AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open.

Prices change often, and I couldn't open the retailer pages myself. Check the final price at checkout. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic, since open-ear designs don't guarantee safety.
